## 8B. MIT-First Licensing and Dependency Concessions ⚖️

- Prefer MIT for new original code when licensing is authorized, except when the owner specifies otherwise or actual third-party terms require another choice. Preserve existing project licenses unless change is justified and authorized.
- Evaluate useful libraries and code on merit as well as their actual licenses. GPL, AGPL, LGPL, or other concessions are acceptable when the associated obligations can be met; do not needlessly reinvent code just to retain MIT.
- Examine relevant copying, linking, modification, distribution, network-service, source-availability, and notice requirements. A copyleft dependency does not automatically relicense every unrelated part of a project; verify the conditions applicable to the integrated work.
- Preserve required notices and provenance, document significant licensing trade-offs, and seek owner authorization before changing an existing repository's overall license. Do not assume or claim unverified legal compatibility.

## 8B. MIT-First Licensing and Dependency Concessions ⚖️

- Prefer MIT for new original code when licensing is authorized, except when the owner specifies otherwise or actual third-party terms require another choice. Preserve existing project licenses unless change is justified and authorized.
- Evaluate useful libraries and code on merit as well as their actual licenses. GPL, AGPL, LGPL, or other concessions are acceptable when the associated obligations can be met; do not needlessly reinvent code just to retain MIT.
- Examine relevant copying, linking, modification, distribution, network-service, source-availability, and notice requirements. A copyleft dependency does not automatically relicense every unrelated part of a project; verify the conditions applicable to the integrated work.
- Preserve required notices and provenance, document significant licensing trade-offs, and seek owner authorization before changing an existing repository's overall license. Do not assume or claim unverified legal compatibility.

- Preserve the existing repository license; prefer MIT for independently owned additions only when legally compatible. Do not relicense a pre-existing project merely to satisfy the preference.
- Accept worthwhile GPL, AGPL, LGPL or differently licensed dependencies when the actual integration and distribution terms can be met. Check obligations and attribution, document important trade-offs, and seek owner approval before changing the project's overall license rather than unnecessarily reimplementing a library.
